analysis: Changed behavior: SSDPrefixCache.evictOldestEntry (patch hunk @@ -1769 in SSDPrefixCache.swift) now delegates victim selection to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:), which is not in the supplied source. The closure still calls retireIndexedEntries([url]) with a URL built from the HMAC-hex tag via SSDBlockStore.fileURL under config.root. The old code's guards (hasSafeRoot check, externalChange abort, indexedBytesFreed accounting, stat eviction increment only when freed>0) are preserved, at least at the call site. The head_text excerpt I examined (scanOnDisk, settleDurableDonation, helpers) is unchanged context. It keeps the symlink and fanout checks, the isSafeBlockURL check, the binding checks, TTL expiry, and the receipt re-read and decrypt before advertising a durable prefix. No change to crypto, lookup-tag derivation (T-041 a/c/d), TTL, disk budget, or epoch handling is visible. Per T-041 notes, eviction must not rotate the epoch; the new test fixtures (SSDOwnedEntryRetirementTests) assert epoch.current and the sequence remain unchanged after eviction, and that external loss and symlink replacement stop eviction, busy files are skipped, a refused epoch deletes nothing, and the fallback is bounded. The other test changes (SSDBlockIndexTests) cover oldestFirstSnapshot ordering and the unsigned tag tie-break. Test files are non-production. Unverified: the implementations of SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, SSDBlockIndex.oldestFirstSnapshot and SSDDiskBudget are outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm the fallback is bounded and does not hold the index lock while the callback runs (a DoS/availability matter, T-016/T-041), and that oldest() and the snapshot share the same ordering. No concrete security regression is identified in the supplied units.
